summary:
During deep-space missions, communication delays of up to 20 minutes make real-time medical support from Earth impossible. To address this, we developed SuitOS: a localized, AI-driven Flight Surgeon built directly into the spacesuit's telemetry loop.

SuitOS processes real-time biometric hardware inputs—including optical webcam extraction and wearable sensor uploads—and monitors them against strict NASA-STD-3001 physiological limits. When anomalies like hypoxia, hyperthermia, or tachycardia are detected, the onboard AI instantly generates offline, actionable emergency medical protocols. This project is critical because it ensures astronaut survivability during communication blackouts, empowering them with autonomous, real-time medical interventions without relying on an Earth-uplink.
details:
SuitOS acts as an autonomous medical assistant inside an astronaut's HUD. The system ingests real-time telemetry across 12 distinct physiological metrics. We integrated multiple hardware input methods to ensure robust monitoring: manual sensor overrides, wearable packet uploads (JSON/CSV), and optical biometric extraction via webcam frame data. The system continuously monitors these baselines against strict NASA-STD-3001 parameters. Upon detecting a critical anomaly, the onboard LLM instantly streams a diagnostic status update and generates two immediate, actionable countermeasures for the astronaut to execute, completely independent of Earth. The impact is enhanced autonomy and survivability for deep-space missions (Mars and beyond).

Tools, Languages, and Software: We built this web application using Python and Streamlit for the responsive, glassmorphism UI. We utilized the OpenAI SDK connected to Groq's API to power the local LLM inference, ensuring lightning-fast response times. The application relies on Pandas for data structuring, session-state caching for zero-reload AI streaming, and the Requests library for real-time NASA API integrations.

Creativity and Factors Considered: We recognized that spaceflight causes extreme psychological stress, so we integrated a "Mental Health & Morale" module that streams live Earth imagery from the ISS Cupola to act as an active psychological countermeasure. Furthermore, we built a fallback failover chain for the AI models to ensure the system remains online even if one model degrades.
